How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 12 Accountancy Part I, Chapter 1 (Accounting for Partnership: Basic Concepts), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. The theory paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, with 20 marks for project work. Part A, Accounting for Partnership Firms, carries 36 marks, and Accounting for Companies carries 24; Part B, Analysis of Financial Statements, carries 12 marks and the Cash Flow Statement 8. Recent sample papers have 34 questions: Part A has 16 one-mark items, four 3-mark, two 4-mark and four 6-mark questions (60 marks); Part B has 4 one-mark items, two 3-mark, one 4-mark and one 6-mark question (20 marks).

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. All figures are invented for practice, and every calculation was checked by computer. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme. Amounts are in rupees (₹), written in the Indian style (₹1,00,000 = one lakh).

Unit 1 of 10: Nature of Partnership and the Partnership Deed

Key ideas

  • Partnership (Indian Partnership Act, 1932, Section 4): "the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all".
  • Features:
  • two or more persons; the maximum is 50 (Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014);
  • an agreement (oral or written);
  • a business carried on with a profit motive;
  • sharing of profits (and losses);
  • mutual agency — each partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners;
  • unlimited liability of partners.
  • Partnership deed: the written agreement. Its usual contents: name and address of the firm and partners; nature of business; date of commencement; duration; capital contribution; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and on drawings; salaries and commission; interest on partners' loans; rules for admission, retirement, death and dissolution; settlement of disputes (arbitration).

Worked examples

Example 1: Is a group of three friends who jointly buy a car for personal use a partnership? Answer: no — there is no business carried on for profit.

Example 2: Why is a partnership deed useful? Answer: it sets out the rights and duties of partners in writing, which prevents and settles disputes.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) The maximum number of partners in a partnership firm is: (a) 10 (b) 20 (c) 50 (d) 100. Answer: (c).
  2. (1 mark) What is meant by "mutual agency"? Answer: each partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners, so the acts of one bind all.
  3. (3 marks) State any three features of a partnership. Answer: any three: agreement between two or more persons (1); business carried on for profit (1); sharing of profits; mutual agency; unlimited liability (1).
  4. (2 marks) Give any four items usually included in a partnership deed. Answer: any four, ½ each: capital contributed; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and drawings; salaries/commission; interest on loans; rules for admission/retirement/dissolution.
  5. (3 marks) "A partnership deed is not compulsory, but it is advisable." Explain. Answer: a partnership can be formed by an oral agreement (1); but disputes may arise about profit sharing, interest, salaries, etc. (1); a written deed records these terms and can be used as evidence to settle disputes (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Saying the maximum is 20 (older rule). 2. Calling a deed compulsory. 3. Forgetting mutual agency. 4. Saying liability is limited. 5. Confusing co-ownership with partnership.

Quick recall

  1. Act governing partnership? 2. Maximum partners? 3. Written agreement? 4. Liability of partners? 5. Essential motive?

Answers: 1) Indian Partnership Act, 1932. 2) 50. 3) Partnership deed. 4) Unlimited. 5) Profit.
